question: Which of the following morphological features do we expect to find in the biopsy of the gastric body of a patient with vitamin B12 deficiency?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "impaired DNA synthesis" -> "atrophy of gastric mucosa" -> "increased risk of atrophic gastritis" -> "atrophy" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "chronic gastritis" -> "possible intestinal metaplasia" -> "unclear" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "increased gastric pH" -> "Helicobacter pylori colonization" -> "possible presence in biopsy" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "hyperplasia of endocrine cells" -> "compensatory response to low intrinsic factor" -> "hyperplasia of endocrine cells" -> 75%
analysis: In patients with vitamin B12 deficiency, particularly due to pernicious anemia, we often observe atrophic gastritis characterized by atrophy of gastric mucosa. This can lead to a decrease in gastric acid production and subsequent changes in the gastric environment. While intestinal metaplasia and hyperplasia of endocrine cells can occur in various gastric pathologies, atrophy is a more direct consequence of the deficiency. Therefore, atrophy is the most expected morphological feature in the biopsy of the gastric body in this context.
